title: Recited at a śrāddha
theme: Whoever, purified, has this supreme secret recited in an assembly of brāhmaṇas or at the time of a śrāddha — that leads to endless fruit. The repeated last words close the first adhyāya.

words.meaning: should cause to be heard, should recite
words.context: Śaṅkara: «ग्रन्थतोऽर्थतश्च», in its words and in its meaning

words.meaning: at the time of a śrāddha

words.role: marks the end of the section

sandhi.type: aḥ before a vowel other than a
sandhi.rule: The visarga after a becomes y before a vowel other than a, P. 8.3.17 (भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि), and the y is dropped, P. 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य), leaving the hiatus ya imam.
A final t becomes d before b, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते).
A final t becomes d before a vowel, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते).
e becomes ay before i, P. 6.1.78 (एचोऽयवायावः), and the y is dropped, P. 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य).

samasa.meaning: an assembly of brāhmaṇas (Śaṅkara's analysis; brahman here stands for the brāhmaṇas)

morphology.note: Optative of the causative of √śru, ‘hear’: ‘should make [others] hear’, that is, recite to them.
The final words are repeated, with iti, to mark the end of the first adhyāya: Śaṅkara, «द्विर्वचनमध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थम्».

translation.literal: Whoever, purified, should cause this supreme secret to be heard in an assembly of brāhmaṇas, or at the time of a śrāddha — that serves for endlessness; that serves for endlessness. Thus.
translation.readable: Whoever, with a pure mind, recites this supreme secret to an assembly of brāhmaṇas, or at the time of the rite for the ancestors — that brings endless fruit. That brings endless fruit.

anvaya: यः प्रयतः [सन्] इमम् परमम् गुह्यम् ब्रह्मसंसदि श्राद्धकाले वा श्रावयेत्, तत् आनन्त्याय कल्पते; तत् आनन्त्याय कल्पते इति ।
syntax: A relative clause (yaḥ … śrāvayet) gives the condition; the main clause tat ānantyāya kalpate gives the result, with the dative of purpose. The main clause is repeated with iti to close the adhyāya. The object of śrāvayet is masculine (imam … guhyam), agreeing with an understood noun; Śaṅkara supplies grantham, ‘text’.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: the śrāddha at which it is recited, «तत् श्राद्धम् अस्य आनन्त्याय अनन्तफलाय कल्पते», brings endless fruit. Raṅgarāmānuja's short comment glosses only the assembly and prayataḥ.

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: Anuṣṭubh, 16 + 16, with the closing repetition tad ānantyāya kalpata iti (10 syllables) added: 16 and 26 as written.

beginner: This verse ends the first half of the Kaṭha. It says that whoever, with a pure mind, recites this supreme secret teaching to a gathering of learned people, or at the time of the rite for the ancestors called śrāddha, gains something endless by it. The last words are said twice. Śaṅkara explains that the repetition simply marks the end of a section, the way a reciter signals that a chapter is complete. He reads ‘that’ as the ancestral rite itself, which becomes endlessly fruitful when the teaching is recited at it. The verse belongs to a common pattern: a teaching closes by praising its own recitation. It reports what the text promises; it says nothing about how such a promise should be understood today, which is left to the reader and to tradition.
analogy: Like the closing line a storyteller repeats at the end of a tale, so that everyone knows it is over.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Whoever, purified, recites this supreme secret in an assembly of brāhmaṇas or at the time of a śrāddha, that leads to endless fruit; the last words are repeated.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: the śrāddha becomes endless; the repetition closes the adhyāya
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Whoever recites this text in its words and in its meaning, «ग्रन्थतोऽर्थतश्च», in an assembly of brāhmaṇas, purified, or at the time of a śrāddha to those eating — «तत् श्राद्धम् अस्य आनन्त्याय अनन्तफलाय कल्पते». The repetition marks the end of the adhyāya: «द्विर्वचनमध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थम्».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: His short comment glosses the assembly of brāhmaṇas, «ब्राह्मणसमाजे», and prayataḥ as pure. His entry for this verse is printed after the colophon of the third vallī and before the colophon of his own comment on it.

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: Repeating the last words of a section is a common way of marking its end in Vedic prose and verse; Śaṅkara says so here. The second adhyāya begins with 2.1.1.

advaita.text: Recitation of the text, in words and meaning, makes a śrāddha endlessly fruitful; the doubled words close the adhyāya.

visistadvaita.text: A brief gloss: the assembly is a gathering of brāhmaṇas, «ब्राह्मणसमाजे»; the reciter is to be pure.

schools.disagreement: None; the verse is a praise of recitation and the commentators gloss it briefly. Madhva's bhāṣya, in our source, has no comment on this verse.

contemporary.text: Remembering the dead with words that matter is an old practice in many cultures. The verse links a teaching about what does not die to the rite that remembers those who have died. Whatever one makes of its promise, the pairing is worth noticing. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Why might a teaching about death and the deathless be fitting at a rite for the dead?
reflect.deeper: Śaṅkara stresses reciting the text ‘in its words and in its meaning’. What is lost when only the words are passed on?
reflect.practice: Choose one verse of this vallī and learn it with its meaning, so that you could explain it to someone else.

flags.note: tat: the śrāddha (Śaṅkara). Madhva's bhāṣya has no comment on the verse; his text writes kalpate iti without sandhi (corrections.json, orthographic).
